title: Tarte Tatin
subtitle: Upside-down caramelised apple tart
excerpt: Apples caramelised in butter and sugar in the pan, topped with a disc of pastry, baked until the pastry is golden, then inverted so the caramelised apples are on top. One of the great French desserts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tarte Tatin was created by the Tatin sisters, Stéphanie and Caroline, at their hotel in Lamotte-Beuvron in the Loire Valley, reputedly by accident around 1889. The story goes that Stéphanie started making a traditional apple tart but left the apples cooking too long in butter and sugar on the stove; to rescue the dish she put the pastry on top and finished it in the oven. The result was presented inverted, and a classic was born. The restaurant Maxim's in Paris helped spread the recipe when they adopted it. The technique has since been applied to other fruits, pears, quince, and tomatoes among them, as well as savoury vegetables.

recipeTools.notes: A 24 cm cast-iron or oven-safe frying pan that can go from hob to oven.

content.text: Use apples that hold their shape during the long caramelisation: Cox, Braeburn, Granny Smith, or any firm, flavourful eating apple. Avoid Golden Delicious, which turns to mush. The inversion is the nerve-wracking moment: do it over the sink in case of drips, use a large plate significantly bigger than the tin, press the plate firmly on top of the tin, then flip in one fast movement. Have oven gloves on: the caramel is extremely hot.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Put the sugar in an even layer in a 24 cm oven-safe frying pan. Heat over medium heat without stirring until the edges begin to melt. Gently swirl (do not stir) until the caramel is an even amber colour. Add the butter and stir briefly until melted. Add the vanilla and cinnamon.

Arrange the apple halves tightly in the caramel, cut-side up, packing them in as they will shrink during cooking. The fit should be very snug. Cook on medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the apples are beginning to soften and the caramel around them is deep amber. Remove from the heat.
Cut a disc of puff pastry slightly larger than the pan. Lay it over the apples, tucking the edges down the sides of the pan. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and crisp.

Remove from the oven and rest for 5 minutes. Place a large plate over the pan. Using oven gloves, invert the pan quickly and firmly onto the plate. Lift the pan off. Rearrange any apples that have moved. Serve warm with crème fraîche or vanilla ice cream.
